_comment: WHICH PROFILE A GIVEN MACHINE SHOULD USE. This file is JUDGEMENT, declared
once, in data. `scripts/otr_machine_matrix.py` VALIDATES every row against
the named profile's own fields and REFUSES to generate on a contradiction --
so the opinion lives here and the facts are enforced mechanically.
IT IS NEVER DERIVED. Several profiles fit any class, and choosing between
them is operator judgement about recipe quality, not arithmetic on a VRAM
number. A generator that computed this would ship guesses carrying the
MEMBERSHIP HERE IS THE AUDIENCE MARKER. A profile is user-facing if and only
if a row below names it. `status` does NOT decide this: 41 profiles are
`shipping` at the 16 GB tier and 18 of them are `otr_w45_*` harness
instruments -- mature, and not something to hand a stranger. A new harness
profile nobody classifies stays internal, which is the safe direction to
`recommended` may be null. A declared gap is better than a rediscovered one.

classes.label: 8 GB NVIDIA (RTX 4060, 3070, 2080)
classes.note: The portability floor. Proven, and the reason it is proven is that a second machine exists.

proven.evidence: docs/4060_DRILL_LOG.md steps 7-19; five of five banks published

classes.label: 16 GB or more NVIDIA (RTX 5080, 3090, 4090, A4500)
classes.note: One class, not three. Nothing sized ABOVE 16 GB was proven, so a 24 GB card runs what a 16 GB card runs. `otr_rented24_heavy` is the draft that asks for more -- unproven, and the instrument the next rental needs. AnimateDiff is the FLOOR lane and belongs to the small-VRAM classes; from 16 GB up the declared engine is real video diffusion. Operator, 2026-09-01: "i dont care about animatediff except for the smallest machines, 16gb vram over i want real video proven". ltx25_high_video is proven on the RTX 5080: two 1-act legs on 2026-09-01, 01:26:19 and 01:52:13, both RESULT SUCCESS. FIND YOUR CARD BY VRAM AND ARCHITECTURE, NOT BY NAME. The proof on this row was measured on an RTX A4500 -- Ampere, compute 8.6, 20 GB -- which most people have never held. What it stands in for is any Ampere-or-newer card with 16 GB or more: a 3090 or 3090 Ti (24 GB, same architecture, more SMs) is covered by it; a 4090 almost certainly is. A 3080 Ti is NOT, despite being the same architecture, because it has 12 GB and belongs to the row below. The class engine is the one proven across the WHOLE class, not the best one on the fastest member: wan22_high_video has published episodes on both Blackwell (RTX 5080) and Ampere (rented A4500), and its weights are publicly fetchable. ltx25_high_video is the better picture on the 5080 and stays in the dropdown, but it has never rendered on any other machine, so advertising it as the class default would tell a 3090 or A4500 owner that a blocked lane is PROVEN.

proven.evidence: continuous overnight 5-act loops published to otr/obs
1-act, 8 clips, 2058 s, peak 15,990 MB, obs_publish OK

animatediff + sci_fi_radio + scifi_news_pro, 1-act: 187.6 s, 1920x1080 h264 + aac, 3621 s render, obs_publish OK. DRAM canary tripped at 1.64 GB available and the blend proceeded anyway -- advisory, not a degrade; the published episode is full quality.

ltx_8gb (LTX-2b-0.9.8-distilled): 9 beats -> 1100 frames, 63.8 s 1920x1080 h264 + aac, 1925 s, obs_publish OK. First meaty video-diffusion lane proven on a NON-Blackwell card. Same run confirmed the architecture-aware image lane: compute_cap 86 selected z_image bf16 over nvfp4, which this card cannot execute.

wan_ti2v (Wan2.2-TI2V-5B GGUF): RESULT SUCCESS in 3949 s, obs_publish OK. Second meaty video lane on a NON-Blackwell card. Required three installs the provisioner now performs: the ComfyUI-GGUF pack, the gguf wheel, and sentencepiece+protobuf -- the last two listed upstream as '# optional - tokenizer' and not optional here.

ltx25_high_video, 1 act: episode signal_lost_feline_visitor_a_space_oddity_20260831_191928, Prompt executed in 01:26:19. The episode's own canon records render engine ltx25_video. First OTR-published LTX 2.5 episode.

classes.label: 10-15 GB NVIDIA (RTX 4070, 3080, 3080 Ti 12 GB)
classes.note: UNTESTED. Sized between the two proven bands rather than absorbed into 16 GB+, which would hand a 12 GB card a 14.5 GB writer ceiling.

classes.label: AMD / ROCm
classes.note: Largely unexplored. The profile exists; no episode has published from it.

defaults._comment: Shared by every machine. A class row states only what makes that machine DIFFERENT. Nothing here lives in a .py file.

known_limits: indextts2 is NOT selectable as the announcer voice -- OTR_CastLock's announcer combo is (auto, kokoro, chatterbox, dia, elevenlabs, google_tts, bark). It IS selectable as the character voice. Recorded here rather than worked around: the dropdown decides, the workflow runs it, and a failure gets written down.
chatterbox and dia are announcer-capable cloning engines but each needs its own isolated venv; neither is installed on the rented pod.
OTR_ImageDirector dtype_policy accepts fp8_ok / no_fp8 / no_fp8_no_fp4 only. 'fp16' is not a choice -- it was invented here once and failed at apply time, which is the intended behaviour.

scifi_news_pro on a rented pod: the RSS bank works, and two wrong diagnoses were recorded here before the right one. It is NOT datacenter IP blocking -- with a real User-Agent, sciencedaily/BBC/MIT all return 200 from the pod and only cosmosmagazine 403s. It is NOT partial feed failure either; the fetcher already skips a refusing feed. The cause was `feedparser` missing from ComfyUI's own venv, declared in requirements.txt and pyproject.toml but installed by the provisioner into the SYSTEM python. Same root as the `accelerate` failure. Fixed in scripts/otr_pod_provision.sh.

voice_bank must match the voice engine: kokoro accepts only 'kokoro_builtin'. Setting 'default' with char_voice=kokoro raises VoiceCastingError at OTR_CastLock, 12 minutes into a leg. Found by running it, 2026-08-31.

ltx25_high_video is PROVEN on the RTX 5080 only, and is a RunPod lab candidate everywhere else -- not proven. Its gemma4-12b encoder is rejected by a stock ComfyUI-GGUF ('Unexpected text model architecture type in GGUF file: gemma4'), and the 17-line loader patch that fixes it is not public. On a rented A4500 with the patch applied it cleared the loader and was then SIGKILLed at the container's 57.7 GiB cgroup limit during the two-stage decode at 1664x960. It is promoted to proven for a second machine only when a pod render publishes an episode.

humo is PROVEN on the RTX 5080 (32 published episodes across humo_14B_169, humo_1.7B_169, humo_1.7B and humo) and is a RunPod lab candidate elsewhere. Every node class resolves on a rented pod with no patching; what is missing is ~27 GiB of weights and a fetch lane. Qualification is queued behind ltx25 on a high-RAM pod.
